newsitem.title: USA: McGraw-Hill results boosted by Shepard's sale.
newsitem.headline: McGraw-Hill results boosted by Shepard's sale.

text.p: McGraw-Hill Cos. Tuesday reported sharply higher fourth-quarter and 1996 earnings, boosted by a $260.5 million gain from the sale of its Shepard's legal citation business.
The New York-based company in October completed the first part of the sale, in exchange for the Times Mirror Co.'s Higher Education Group, in October.

McGraw-Hill said its net income surged to $307.87 million, or $3.08 a share, in the quarter from $54.5 million, or 54 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Operating revenues rose to $830.9 million from $749.6 million.
For the full-year, net income jumped to $495.7 million, or $4.96 a share, from $227.1 million, or $2.28 a share, in 1995. Operating revenues rose to $3.07 billion from $2.9 billion.

The results include an after-tax gain of $2.61 a share for the sale of Shepard's. McGraw-Hill also took a charge of $14.9 million, or 15 cents a share, to integrate the College division with the higher education business.
The company's stock edged up 37.5 cents to $48.875 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
